---
title: "An error message does not say where the call came from"
ref: FUN-09
categories: [Functions]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "an error that mentions `fun2()` and the value received"
versions: "All"
source: "safer-r"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
fun1 <- function(x) {
  if (x == 0) {
    bob
  } else {
    x
  }
}
fun2 <- function(x) {
  fun1(x)
}
fun2(0)
```
:::

## Why

The error message only cites the call where the error happened, here `fun1()`. You know neither that `fun2()` was the caller, nor which value of `x` triggered the problem.

In an interactive console, `traceback()` lets you recover the call stack. In a script run as a scheduled task, or in a loop over hundreds of items, that message is often all that is left.

## The remedy

Add context where you know it, by catching the error and raising it again with a complete message.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
fun2 <- function(x) {
  tryCatch(fun1(x), error = function(e) {
    stop("fun2() failed for x = ", x, ": ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
  })
}
fun2(0)
```
:::
